title: I Will Praise Thee Every Day
description: I Will Praise Thee Every Day in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 58, “O Lord, I will praise thee! Isa 12”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: I Will praise thee ev-ery day Now thine an-ger's turned a-way! Com-fort-a-ble thoughts a-rise From the bleed-ing sac-ri-fice.

lines: I Will praise thee every day
Now thine anger's turned away!
Comfortable thoughts arise
From the bleeding sacrifice.
Here in the fair gospel field,
Wells of free salvation yield
Streams of life, a plenteous store,
And my soul shall thirst no more.
Jesus is become at length
My salvation and my strength;
And his praises shall prolong,
While I live, my pleasant song.
Praise ye, then, his glorious name,
Publish his exalted fame!
Still his worth your praise exceeds,
Excellent are all his deeds.
Raise again the joyful sound,
Let the nations roll it round!
Zion shout, for this is he,
God the Savior dwells in thee.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
